job.title: Head Orthoptist
job.description:
MAYDAY Healthcare is proud to be partnering with a leading multi-subspecialty ophthalmology clinic located in Sydney Eastern Suburbs.

This highly regarded practice is home to a team of respected ophthalmologists and experienced clinical professionals who are passionate about delivering exceptional patient care across the full spectrum of eye health.

We are seeking an experienced Head Orthoptist to lead and develop a team of Orthoptists while partnering closely with ophthalmologists to drive clinical excellence, operational efficiency, and exceptional patient outcomes.

Offering a salary of up to $140,000 + Super, this is an outstanding opportunity for an accomplished Orthoptist to step into a key leadership position where they can influence team culture, shape clinical standards, and support the development of the next generation of Orthoptists.

What's on Offer

  • Salary up to $140,000 + Super
  • Genuine leadership opportunity within a well-established specialist practice
  • Lead, mentor and develop a team of 3-4 Orthoptists
  • Play a key role in onboarding, training and developing future Orthoptists
  • Opportunity to shape clinical standards, policies and procedures
  • Work closely with highly respected ophthalmologists and practice leaders
  • Exposure across a broad range of ophthalmology subspecialties
  • Supportive and collaborative team culture
  • Metro location with onsite parking available and close proximity to train and public transport options
  • Ongoing professional development opportunities

The Role

As Head Orthoptist, you will combine hands-on clinical responsibilities with leadership and operational oversight, acting as a key link between the Orthoptist team, specialists and practice leadership.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Leading, mentoring and developing a team of 3-4 Orthoptists
  • Supporting the onboarding, training and professional growth of new team members
  • Creating, reviewing and implementing clinical policies and procedures
  • Driving consistency, quality and best-practice standards across the clinic
  • Working closely with ophthalmologists to support exceptional patient outcomes
  • Managing clinic flow and ensuring efficient day-to-day operations
  • Providing leadership, guidance and support within a busy clinical environment
  • Conducting comprehensive patient assessments and consultations
  • Performing and overseeing ophthalmic diagnostic testing
  • Supporting pre-operative and post-operative patient care
  • Assisting with clinical audits, quality improvement initiatives and compliance requirements
  • Building strong relationships across the wider multidisciplinary team
  • Identifying opportunities to improve workflows, patient experience and team performance

About You

We're looking for a natural leader who is calm under pressure, empathetic with their team and patients, yet confident enough to provide clear direction and uphold standards when required.

You'll bring:

  • Qualification as an Orthoptist with current Australian registration
  • Significant experience within an ophthalmology setting
  • Previous leadership, mentoring or senior clinical experience
  • A calm, empathetic and professional leadership style
  • The confidence to make decisions and have difficult conversations when required
  • Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to work collaboratively with specialists and support teams
  • A passion for coaching, developing and supporting others
  • Excellent organisational, communication and stakeholder management skills
  • Experience developing or working within policies, procedures and clinical governance frameworks
  • A proactive approach with the ability to balance clinical and operational responsibilities

Why This Opportunity?

This role offers far more than a traditional senior Orthoptist position.

You'll have the opportunity to influence team culture, develop future Orthoptists, strengthen clinical standards, and become a trusted partner to a highly respected group of ophthalmologists. We are looking for someone with the emotional intelligence to support and grow a team, the resilience to navigate challenges, and the leadership capability to drive continuous improvement across the service.

If you're looking for a leadership role where you can make a genuine impact while remaining clinically involved, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Paediatric Occupational Therapist

Permanent Part-Time | Marsden Park, Box Hill & Surrounding Areas | $105,000–$115,000 + Super FTE, Pro Rata

MAYDAY Healthcare is partnering with a growing paediatric allied health practice to find an experienced Occupational Therapist who is ready to take ownership of their caseload, work autonomously and play a genuine role in shaping the future of a growing business.

This is a rare opportunity to join a small, family-focused practice where you’re not just another clinician on a productivity spreadsheet. You’ll have the freedom to manage your own calendar, build strong relationships with families and have a real say in how you work.

With a strong referral network and an established waitlist, you’ll step into an existing caseload rather than spending months trying to build one.

Why You’ll Love This Role

  • Take ownership of your own caseload and calendar
  • Start with an established client base — no need to build a caseload from scratch
  • No rigid billable-hour or productivity targets
  • Geographically sensible caseloads designed to minimise unnecessary travel
  • Flexibility to structure your working day around your clients and your preferred working style
  • Work across homes, schools, childcare centres, preschools and community settings
  • No weekend or evening work
  • Opportunity to increase your days and responsibilities as the practice grows
  • Potential future pathway into senior or clinical leadership

The Role
Working approximately 3 days per week, you’ll independently manage your own paediatric caseload across Marsden Park, Box Hill and surrounding suburbs.
You’ll be trusted to manage your own:

  • Calendar and appointments
  • Client communication
  • Clinical documentation
  • Assessments and reports
  • Therapy planning
  • Relationships with families and other professionals

Your Clients
The caseload is predominantly children aged approximately 2.5–13 years, with a strong focus on neurodivergent and autistic children.
You’ll support clients across areas including:

  • Autism and neurodivergence
  • Developmental delay
  • ADHD
  • Sensory regulation
  • Emotional regulation
  • Fine and gross motor development
  • Self-care and daily living skills
  • Functional and developmental assessments

You’ll also work alongside Speech Pathologists, Behavioural Therapists, Paediatricians, educators and other allied health professionals.

About You
We’re looking for a Paediatric OT who is clinically confident and genuinely enjoys having autonomy.
Ideally, you’ll bring:

  • 3–5+ years of paediatric OT experience
  • Current AHPRA registration
  • Strong autism/neurodivergent experience
  • Confidence managing an independent caseload
  • Strong assessment and report-writing skills
  • Excellent family and stakeholder communication
  • Strong organisation and follow-through
  • A warm, empathetic and family-centred approach
  • Comfort working independently in the community
  • Current driver's licence and access to a suitable vehicle
  • Current NSW Working With Children Check
  • National Police Check
  • First Aid and CPR certification
  • NDIS experience highly regarded

A Practice That Puts People First
The practice is built around a genuinely family-centred and neuroaffirming approach.

Rather than taking a one-size-fits-all approach, you'll have the freedom to understand each child and family, work towards meaningful goals and deliver practical therapy that fits into everyday life.

You'll be joining a small team where your ideas are heard, your clinical judgement is trusted and your work can have a direct impact on the continued growth of the practice.

What’s On Offer

  • $105,000–$115,000 + super FTE, pro rata
  • Permanent part-time, ideally 3 days per week
  • Flexible working arrangement
  • Established caseload from day one
  • No billable-hour targets
  • No unnecessary productivity pressure
  • Autonomy over your calendar and caseload
  • Geographically concentrated client base
  • Regular clinical support and supervision
  • Direct access to the practice owner
  • No weekends or evenings
  • Opportunity to increase days over time
  • Genuine opportunity to help shape a growing practice
  • Potential future senior/clinical leadership opportunities

If you're an experienced Paediatric OT who wants more autonomy, less corporate pressure and the opportunity to genuinely take ownership of your work, this could be the role for you.

Apply now or contact MAYDAY Healthcare for a confidential discussion.
